Selectable generated-media engines are a narrower subset: OpenAI API-key `gpt-image-2`, Responses `image_generation`, mandatory OpenAI/Codex subscription-backed image generation, MiniMax global `image-01`, Gemini Direct generated-image routes where verified, and the separate capability-gated Antigravity OAuth/internal `gemini-3.1-flash-image` route where locally proven. Each entry:
- `id` (string, required): stable capability identifier.
- `category` (string, required): `"media"` or `"provider_tool"`.
- `enabled` (bool, required): whether the capability is currently usable.
- `disabled_reason` (string | null, required): one of the canonical disabled-reason values (§1.3) when `enabled` is `false`; `null` when `enabled` is `true`.
- `setup_hint` (string | null, optional): human-readable guidance for resolving the disabled state.

items.impact: Runtime callers and the picker cannot faithfully distinguish capability-gated, unverified, unsupported, separate-profile, or source-lineage-only rows, inviting lossy boolean projection and misleading availability.
items.statement: The required support states, verification state, provenance, account/profile distinctions, and per-modality route truth have no fields in the defined `capabilities.get` entry shape, which exposes only id, category, enabled, one disabled reason, and an optional hint.
items.title: Capability response cannot represent the required route taxonomy

evidence.exact_quote:
Required routing order:
1. resolve the requested provider/runtime surface for media
2. resolve the requested/effective auth family and eligible account or profile set
3. choose the concrete runtime surface that actually supports the requested media kind
4. record the resulting requested/effective runtime snapshot
2. resolve the requested/effective auth family and eligible account or profile set

items.impact: Identical requests can choose different billing, terms, model, or artifact behavior across implementations, and retries may silently cross authority boundaries.
items.statement: Routing says to choose a concrete runtime surface after resolving an eligible account/profile set, but gives no ordering for multiple eligible routes or accounts, no cost/quality/health preference, and no cross-route retry/fallback policy.
items.title: Eligible route and account selection lacks a deterministic tie-break

evidence.exact_quote: Media generation consumes the product-wide shared runtime identity model instead of defining feature-local runtime-state fields. The requested/effective runtime snapshot remains that shared model's one canonical truth for requested/effective runtime state across the product, and media routing reads it to produce less schema drift, better audit/history/debugging (`/history/debugging`), more consistent UI across chat, tools, logs, subagents, and providers, safer routing/retry/account-switch (`/retry/account-switch`) behavior, and fewer feature-local special-case fields. Media-specific records may attach media request/output details, but they must not own or create shadow fields for account, provider, retry, switch, or audit identity.

- multi-project, lane-based orchestration means media records cannot assume one active `/worktree/thread` context; generated artifacts and usage joins must carry enough project, lane, worktree, thread, and request identity to disambiguate concurrent media work.
- The common envelope contract is not optional: media generation records must name request, runtime, usage, route, artifact, and recovery fields explicitly instead of relying on underspecified shared envelope prose.

items.impact: Audit, usage attribution, account-switch safety, concurrent project disambiguation, and recovery cannot be reconstructed from the specified response or manifest.
items.statement: The prose forbids feature-local identity shadows and requires explicit request, runtime, usage, route, artifact, and recovery fields plus multi-project/lane/worktree/thread identity, but the response engine exposes only three route identifiers and no requested/effective auth, account, project, lane, thread, retry, switch, or recovery identity.
items.title: Required shared runtime and common envelope identity is absent from the response

evidence.exact_quote: `media.generate` is the uniform internal tool for all media generation. It accepts a structured request envelope and returns media output or an error.

**Concurrent requests:** Multiple `media.generate` calls may execute concurrently as long as each uses its own `request_id` directory. No request may append into another request's directory. Retry behavior MUST allocate a new `request_id` rather than mutating a previous manifest in place.

items.impact: Double submission, timeout ambiguity, and network retry can generate duplicate billable media and orphan work with no reliable deduplication or cancellation recovery.
items.statement: The uniform synchronous request envelope defines no idempotency key, cancellation token/state, deadline, polling handle, or client-disconnect behavior; retries always allocate a new request ID without a parent-attempt link.
items.title: Request lifecycle lacks idempotency, cancellation, and deadline semantics

  ```

  ```

  - `image`: `\b(image|picture|photo|logo|poster|thumbnail|cover)\b`
  - `video`: `\b(video|clip|animation|broll|b-roll)\b`
  - `tts`: `\b(tts|text to speech|read aloud|say this|voiceover|voice-over)\b`
  - `music`: `\b(music|song|beat|instrumental|soundtrack)\b`
- **Verb fallback** — only if the above are unambiguous (single kind match).
- **Verb fallback** — only if the above are unambiguous (single kind match).

items.impact: Different parsers can route the same user request to image or video generation, potentially creating the wrong billable artifact.
items.statement: Prefix priority is defined, but keyword detection gives no tie-break, rejection, or clarification behavior when a prompt contains more than one kind, such as 'make a video from this image'; the unambiguous guard is stated only for verb fallback.
items.title: Multi-kind prompts have no deterministic outcome

evidence.exact_quote: (?is)\b(?:using|with|via|use|model)\s*(?:[:=]\s*)?(?P<model>@?[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._/\-\s]{0,80}?)(?=(?:\s*(?:,|;|\)|\]|\.$|$))|\s+\b(?:for|aspect|ratio|size|resolution|format|voice|duration|negative|quality|seed|bpm|variations?|versions?|options?)\b)

**Normalize model key:** lowercase; collapse spaces, underscores, and hyphens.

**Resolution order:** alias → exact model id → exact displayName → else `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`.

items.impact: Benign prompts can fail with MODEL_UNAVAILABLE or route to an unintended model, and collisions can resolve differently by registry order.
items.statement: Treating bare `with` and `using` as model introducers lets ordinary prompts such as 'image: a cat with blue eyes' capture creative text as a model override; alias-first resolution plus normalization also lacks collision handling when an alias shadows an exact model ID or multiple names normalize identically.
items.title: Broad model extraction can consume ordinary creative prose

evidence.exact_quote:
(?i)\b(?:(?:make|generate|create|give me|output|render)\s+)?(?P<count>\d{1,2})\s*(?:x\s*)?(?:variations?|versions?|options?|images?|pics?|pictures?|clips?|frames?)\b
```

Optional word forms (one through ten) follow the same pattern. Clamp to safe max (default 8). Last match wins.

items.impact: Invalid or unsupported values may be silently clamped, reach providers inconsistently, or trigger avoidable paid failures; conformance tests have no expected outcomes.
items.statement: Count accepts two digits including zero, aspect ratio accepts arbitrary one- or two-digit sides including zero, seed permits ten digits, BPM permits 00 through 999, and duration permits up to 999 seconds, but the grammar specifies no minima, overflow behavior, ratio support check, or provider-specific validation before billing.
items.title: Parsed numeric controls lack local and route-aware validity bounds

```

evidence.exact_quote:
## Appendix A. Slot extraction rules (regex-ish, deterministic)

1) Pre-processing:
- Keep raw (original) and s_lower (normalized lowercased).
- If trailing controls block exists (ends with (...) or [...] and contains control tokens), split body + controls and parse controls first; remove block from prompt.
Controls-block regex: (?is)^(?P<body>.*?)(?:\s*(?P<bracket>\(|\[)\s*(?P<controls>[^)\]]{1,400})\s*(?:\)|\])\s*)$
Control token gate: \b(model|aspect|ratio|size|resolution|duration|voice|format|bpm|seed|negative|quality)\b

15) prompt cleaning:
- If controls block present: remove it.
- Remove only matched spans introduced by control keywords (using/model/size/aspect/etc).
- Preserve remaining text as the creative prompt.

items.title: Duplicated grammar appendix can drift and lacks adversarial fixtures
